about: The gospel of the First Sunday of Advent, Luke 21:25–33. The year opens with the signs before the coming of the Son of Man and with the parable of the fig tree. In illo témpore, At that time, is the missal's own opening and is not part of the verse.

seg.tr: At that time Jesus said to His disciples: There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and on earth distress among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and waves. People will faint from fear and from expectation of what is coming upon the whole world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

fn.w019: The clause has no expressed verb. Erunt from the opening is understood again: there will be distress.
fn.w023: A genitive depending on “confusióne” (w022). In turn, “maris” (w024) and “flúctuum” (w026) depend on “sónitus”.
fn.w027: With “homínibus” (w028), it forms an ablative absolute: while people faint.
fn.w033: A neuter plural pronoun serving as the subject of “supervénient” (w034): the things that will come upon.

seg.tr: Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with great power and majesty.
But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.

fn.w054: With incipientibus it begins an ablative absolute: when these things begin to happen.
fn.w057: The neuter agreement is with his. The infinitive fieri supplies what is beginning to occur.

seg.tr: He told them a parable: Look at the fig tree and all the trees. When they begin to bear fruit, you know that summer is near.

fn.w072: The feminine adjective stands substantivally with arbor understood. The following “omnes” (w074) and “árbores” (w075) broaden the example from the fig tree to all trees.

seg.tr: So too, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.

fn.w091: Future perfect in a future temporal clause: when these things have occurred, the command scitóte follows.

seg.tr: Amen, I tell you: This generation will not pass away until all things come to pass.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will not pass away.
